passages.heading: Day 1 — The Mask
passages.text:

passages.heading: The Mask Off
passages.text:
1. Take 5 minutes alone.
2. Say aloud: "In anger, part of me feels ____ and I don't say it."
3. Fill in the blank three times.
4. Do not fix. Notice.

passages.heading: The Mirror Person
passages.text:
1. Name a person who irritates you around anger.
2. Name the specific trait.
3. Ask honestly: where do I do a subtle version of that?
4. Sit with the mirror.

passages.heading: Meet The Child
passages.text:
1. Bring the sharpest edge of anger to mind.
2. Ask: at what age did this first appear?
3. Speak to that child version silently. "You did well."
4. Sit with them 3 minutes.

passages.heading: The Shadow Gift
passages.text:
1. Name your anger's shadow one word (anger, envy, fear, shame).
2. Ask: what is it trying to protect or point at?
3. Write the answer in one line.
4. Say thank you before you release it.

passages.heading: One Confession
passages.text:
1. Choose one safe person.
2. Share one sentence about anger you've never spoken.
3. Do not defend it. Just say it.
4. Notice what shifts.

passages.heading: Council Of Selves
passages.text:
1. Imagine a table with all your parts around it — the seeker, the achiever, the shadow of anger.
2. Give each a chair.
3. Ask the shadow: what do you want us to remember?
4. Thank it.

passages.heading: Monthly Check
passages.text:
1. On the first Sunday of every month, sit for 10 minutes.
2. Ask: what is anger's shadow doing right now?
3. Listen. Do not fix.
4. Write one line and file it.

1. Choose one safe person.
2. Share one sentence about success fear you've never spoken.
3. Do not defend it. Just say it.
4. Notice what shifts.

passages.heading: Council Of Selves
passages.text:
1. Imagine a table with all your parts around it — the seeker, the achiever, the shadow of success fear.
2. Give each a chair.
3. Ask the shadow: what do you want us to remember?
4. Thank it.

passages.heading: Monthly Check
passages.text:
1. On the first Sunday of every month, sit for 10 minutes.
2. Ask: what is success fear's shadow doing right now?
3. Listen. Do not fix.
4. Write one line and file it.

passages.heading: The Mask Off
passages.text:
1. Take 5 minutes alone.
2. Say aloud: "In dependency, part of me feels ____ and I don't say it."
3. Fill in the blank three times.
4. Do not fix. Notice.

passages.heading: The Mirror Person
passages.text:
1. Name a person who irritates you around dependency.
2. Name the specific trait.
3. Ask honestly: where do I do a subtle version of that?
4. Sit with the mirror.

passages.heading: Meet The Child
passages.text:
1. Bring the sharpest edge of dependency to mind.
2. Ask: at what age did this first appear?
3. Speak to that child version silently. "You did well."
4. Sit with them 3 minutes.

passages.heading: The Shadow Gift
passages.text:
1. Name your dependency's shadow one word (anger, envy, fear, shame).
2. Ask: what is it trying to protect or point at?
3. Write the answer in one line.
4. Say thank you before you release it.

passages.heading: One Confession
passages.text:
1. Choose one safe person.
2. Share one sentence about dependency you've never spoken.
3. Do not defend it. Just say it.
4. Notice what shifts.

passages.heading: Council Of Selves
passages.text:
1. Imagine a table with all your parts around it — the seeker, the achiever, the shadow of dependency.
2. Give each a chair.
3. Ask the shadow: what do you want us to remember?
4. Thank it.

passages.heading: Monthly Check
passages.text:

2. Ask: what is dependency's shadow doing right now?
3. Listen. Do not fix.
4. Write one line and file it.

passages.heading: Return To Play

passages.heading: Locate the Charge
passages.text:
1. Sit. Close your eyes.
2. Name the situation of stage fright out loud in one sentence.
3. Scan the body top to bottom. Where does the sensation live? Jaw? Chest? Belly?
4. Rest attention there for 60 seconds. Don't fix it. Meet it.

passages.heading: 4-8 Breath
passages.text:
Inhale 4 counts through the nose.
Exhale 8 counts through slightly pursed lips.
Repeat for 10 rounds.
Use this in the first 90 seconds of any stage fright spike.

passages.heading: Wide-Angle Attention
passages.text:
1. Close eyes. Hear the furthest sound you can.
2. Feel the weight of your body on the chair.
3. Feel the air on your skin.
4. Now, from this wider place, look at stage fright again. It shrinks.

passages.heading: Precise Naming
passages.text:
1. Feel the current wave of stage fright.
2. Ask: is it fear, grief, anger, shame, or overwhelm?
3. Get more specific: is it fear of being seen, fear of failing, fear of being alone?
4. Say the precise name out loud. Notice what changes.

passages.heading: Shake It Off
passages.text:
1. Stand up.
2. Shake hands, arms, legs, whole body for 90 seconds. Loose.
3. Then still. Feel the aliveness under the skin.
4. Sit and notice how stage fright has changed.

passages.heading: Build Your Anchor
passages.text:
1. Pick one physical gesture (hand on chest, thumb & finger together, feet firmly planted).
2. Sit calmly and combine it with 3 slow breaths.
3. Repeat 5 times so the pairing sets.
4. Use it once today in real life.

passages.heading: Design Your Minimum
passages.text:
1. Of this week's practices, pick one that took under 3 minutes.
2. Attach it to something you already do daily (morning coffee, closing laptop).
3. Commit to 30 days of that pairing.
4. Write it on paper. Put it where you'll see it.

passages.heading: Locate the Charge
passages.text:
1. Sit. Close your eyes.
2. Name the situation of comedown out loud in one sentence.
3. Scan the body top to bottom. Where does the sensation live? Jaw? Chest? Belly?
4. Rest attention there for 60 seconds. Don't fix it. Meet it.

passages.heading: 4-8 Breath
passages.text:
Inhale 4 counts through the nose.
Exhale 8 counts through slightly pursed lips.
Repeat for 10 rounds.
Use this in the first 90 seconds of any comedown spike.

passages.heading: Wide-Angle Attention
passages.text:
1. Close eyes. Hear the furthest sound you can.
2. Feel the weight of your body on the chair.
3. Feel the air on your skin.
4. Now, from this wider place, look at comedown again. It shrinks.

passages.heading: Precise Naming
passages.text:
1. Feel the current wave of comedown.
2. Ask: is it fear, grief, anger, shame, or overwhelm?
3. Get more specific: is it fear of being seen, fear of failing, fear of being alone?
4. Say the precise name out loud. Notice what changes.

passages.heading: Shake It Off
passages.text:
1. Stand up.
2. Shake hands, arms, legs, whole body for 90 seconds. Loose.
3. Then still. Feel the aliveness under the skin.
4. Sit and notice how comedown has changed.

passages.heading: Build Your Anchor
passages.text:
1. Pick one physical gesture (hand on chest, thumb & finger together, feet firmly planted).
2. Sit calmly and combine it with 3 slow breaths.
3. Repeat 5 times so the pairing sets.
4. Use it once today in real life.

passages.heading: Design Your Minimum
passages.text:
1. Of this week's practices, pick one that took under 3 minutes.
2. Attach it to something you already do daily (morning coffee, closing laptop).
3. Commit to 30 days of that pairing.
4. Write it on paper. Put it where you'll see it.

passages.text:

passages.heading: Design The Container
passages.text:
1. Pick a 45-minute slot 4 days a week.
2. Same seat, same light, same drink.
3. Show up empty.
4. Do not judge output for 30 days.

passages.heading: Three Limits
passages.text:
1. Pick three constraints for tomorrow's first book session (word count, palette, time, one instrument).
2. Write them down.
3. Work inside them.
4. Notice the release.

passages.heading: Deliberate Copy
passages.text:

2. Copy it, honestly.
3. Then change one variable.
4. Notice what emerges.

passages.heading: The Small Ship

1. Pick one first book thing 80% done.
2. Ship it today. Small audience is fine.
3. Do not polish more.
4. Note how the body feels post-release.

passages.heading: Name The Critic

2. Assign it a role (edit phase only).
3. Politely bar it from draft phase.

passages.heading: Return To Play
passages.text:
1. Recall the earliest joy first book gave you.
2. Do a 20-minute session in that spirit today.
3. No goal. No audience.
4. Notice.

passages.heading: Attention Audit
passages.text:
1. For one waking hour, log every device pickup.
2. Beside each, write: cue, duration, aftermath.
3. Look for the pattern that surprises you.
4. Name the biggest leak in one word.

passages.heading: One-Tab Hour
passages.text:
1. Pick one 60-minute block today.
2. One tab. One task. Phone in another room.
3. When distraction rises, note it on paper, return.
4. End: notice quality difference.

passages.heading: 10 Breaths
passages.text:
1. Sit or stand.
2. Count 10 breaths in and out, only.
3. Lose count? Restart. No punishment.
4. Use before every photography session for the rest of the week.

passages.heading: Sit With Nothing
passages.text:
1. Sit for 5 minutes with no input. No music. No phone.
2. Watch what the mind does at minute 2 and 4.
3. Do not resolve. Notice.
4. Return to photography refreshed.

passages.heading: Sleep Contract
passages.text:
1. Choose a lights-out time you can hold 5 nights in a row.
2. 60 minutes before: no work, no fast content.
3. 30 minutes before: dim lights.
4. Track it. Sleep is training.

passages.heading: Design The Field
passages.text:
1. Clear one surface entirely.
2. Put one object of intent on it (book, note, image).
3. Remove one visible distraction.
4. Work from this field tomorrow morning.

passages.heading: Stop At 90%
passages.text:
1. In your next work block, set a timer for 25 minutes.
2. Stop when it rings, even if you're mid-sentence.
3. Walk for 5 minutes.
4. Return with fuller attention.
